notes: Not a poll.py backfill: The San Francisco Standard's July 2026 archive was read by Meta Muse, an external reader Stan delegated it to, before he stopped that backfill. Muse returned seven findings and one coverage row. Each article was re-fetched on 2026-11-18 to check its <h1> headline, date and quoted text against the page before anything was written here; Muse's own wording was not used. No backfill window is recorded in state/cursors.json, because the screen did not run on this month.

coverage.remaining: Muse reports listing 269 July 2026 Standard stories and reading 38; the other 231 were judged by Muse from their headlines and are not recorded per item. Muse skipped 31 read stories, nearly all paywalled with no street address in the readable part (Parkmerced, Marina and Fillmore Safeways, Jollibee, Ilna, Florecita, Fieldwork Brewing, Oasis, Shuggie's, Mellow and others); one, a coffee-shop story whose headline names a private person, was skipped outright. A poll.py backfill of this window would reach them again.
coverage.note: Every Standard article read was paywalled after the lede or first section.

findings.description: The distressed sale of the shuttered San Francisco Centre mall, agreed with the winning bidders in March, was called off after due diligence, putting the roughly 1.2 million-square-foot property back on the market. The article names the mall but prints no street number; the site files the mall at 865 Market Street, which already carries the later buyer selection (Chronicle, 22 Oct 2026) and the redevelopment loan (The Registry, 9 Nov 2026). This collapse in July is a separate, earlier event.

findings.description: The Planning Commission unanimously approved an eight-storey, 85-foot condominium building at 230 Anza Street on Thursday 23 July 2026, replacing a vacant structure to be demolished; the first project approved under the Family Zoning Plan. C.M. Wong Architecture designed it. The page already carries San Francisco YIMBY's plans (5 Mar), renderings ahead of this hearing (7 Jul) and building permits (18 Oct); the approval is a distinct event between them.
